html:
The E'ñepá, called Panare by outsiders, are a Cariban speaking people of the Cuchivero and Suapure rivers in Bolívar state, Venezuela, south of the Orinoco. They number several thousand.

They live by farming manioc and maize, hunting with blowguns and shotguns, and making baskets that they sell in local markets. They avoided close contact with outsiders until the mid 1900s, when ranchers and missionaries moved into their land. Their neighbours include the Ye'kuana and the Piaroa, and the Yanomami further south.
